<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917817_theRebbe_541" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917817_theRebbe_541__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Although the level of transformation (It'hapcha) is generally higher than suppression (It'kafya), suppression has a unique advantage in that it specifically draws down the hidden treasure of the Awtsmoos, as illustrated by the parable of a king who spends all his treasures to win a war.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, although the aspect of It'hapcha (transformation) is,</t>
    <t s="2">in general,</t>
    <t s="3">far more elevated than the aspect of It'kafya (suppression),</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless, there is also an advantage in the aspect of It'kafya over the aspect of It'hapcha.</t>
    <t s="5">This is understood from what is said in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="6">that the concept of a "servant of G-d" is specifically when he suppresses and changes his nature,</t>
    <t s="7">and this advantage is not present in a complete tzaddik.</t>
    <t s="8">And specifically through the service of It'kafya, "the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all worlds,"</t>
    <t s="9">the drawing down and revelation of the light that is in the aspect of loftiness,</t>
    <t s="10">as is explained at length in the discourse of the day of the Hilula,</t>
    <t s="11">with a parable of a mortal king who, for the sake of victory in war, spends all his treasures,</t>
    <t s="12">for in normal years, not only does he not use them for anything, but they are hidden and sealed from the eye of any beholder,</t>
    <t s="13">and specifically at the time of war, not only does he open all the treasures,</t>
    <t s="14">but moreover, he spends them without any measure or limit, and gives them to the soldiers in order to win the war.</t>
    <t s="15">And the analogy for this Above,</t>
    <t s="16">is that there is an aspect of a treasure that is hidden and sealed from the eye of any beholder,</t>
    <t s="17">"No eye has seen, O G-d, besides You,"</t>
    <t s="18">and in order to win the war against the evil inclination,</t>
    <t s="19">the service of It'kafya,</t>
    <t s="20">they also give this treasure,</t>
    <t s="21">and in a manner of squandering,</t>
    <t s="22">and the giving of the treasure is specifically to the simple soldiers,</t>
    <t s="23">for since their service is with self-sacrifice beyond the measure and limit of intellect, therefore the giving of the treasure to them is also in a manner of squandering beyond all measure and limit.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>In the future, the Exodus from Egypt will still be mentioned because the advantage of It'kafya—drawing down the hidden treasure—will be needed, and it will be revealed in its ultimate perfection.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Based on this, one can understand why they will mention the Exodus from Egypt even in the future,</t>
    <t s="1">even though the revelations of the future are more elevated</t>
    <t s="2">(wondrous)</t>
    <t s="3">than the revelations that were in the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="4">for since the drawing down of the aspect of the treasure is specifically for the sake of victory in war,</t>
    <t s="5">and in the future there will be no war with the evil inclination, for "the spirit of impurity I will remove from the earth,"</t>
    <t s="6">therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">they will mention the Exodus from Egypt even then,</t>
    <t s="8">in order that there will also be the advantage of It'kafya,</t>
    <t s="9">the drawing down of the aspect of the treasure.</t>
    <t s="10">And this drawing down will also be in ultimate revelation then</t>
    <t s="11">(like all matters of the future),</t>
    <t s="12">and "your Teacher will no longer be hidden."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The future redemption will combine both advantages—the suppression (It'kafya) of the Exodus and the transformation (It'hapcha) of wondrous revelations—achieved through our service in exile with self-sacrifice, leading to a revelation without garments and from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="2">that in the future redemption there will be both advantages,</t>
    <t s="3">the advantage of It'kafya,</t>
    <t s="4">"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="5">and the advantage of It'hapcha,</t>
    <t s="6">"I will show him wonders."</t>
    <t s="7">For through our deeds and service during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="8">the general service of the time of exile being in a manner of self-sacrifice beyond measure and limit,</t>
    <t s="9">for in the time of exile, and especially in the footsteps of Moshiach, there are obstacles and hindrances and many trials,</t>
    <t s="10">even to the trial of not being ashamed before people who mock him,</t>
    <t s="11">and nevertheless, they pay no attention to all the hindrances,</t>
    <t s="12">and they study Torah and fulfill mitzvos without any calculations,</t>
    <t s="13">to the extent that even "the empty ones among you are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate,"</t>
    <t s="14">meaning not only do they fulfill mitzvos, but they are full of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="15">behold, through this they leave exile with great wealth of mitzvos and great wealth of Torah</t>
    <t s="16">[for Torah study is also a mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="17">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="18">it is equivalent to all the mitzvos],</t>
    <t s="19">and since this</t>
    <t s="20">(the great wealth of Torah and mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="21">adds to merit, it also adds haste to "I will hasten it,"</t>
    <t s="22">and in a manner of "behold, with the clouds of heaven,"</t>
    <t s="23">that very soon there will be the true and complete redemption,</t>
    <t s="24">and in a manner of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders," meaning there will be both advantages.</t>
    <t s="25">For since the redemption comes through our deeds and service during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="26">and especially in the footsteps of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="27">therefore it will be "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="28">the advantage of It'kafya,</t>
    <t s="29">and together with this there will also be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="30">wonders even relative to the wonders</t>
    <t s="31">(signs and wonders)</t>
    <t s="32">that were in the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="33">including also the wonders that were at the time of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds,</t>
    <t s="34">for although at the Splitting of the Sea there were most elevated revelations,</t>
    <t s="35">as "each one pointed with his finger and said, 'This is my G-d, and I will glorify Him,'"</t>
    <t s="36">to the extent that "a maidservant saw at the sea what the prophets did not see,"</t>
    <t s="37">nevertheless, all this was at the sea,</t>
    <t s="38">clothed in the aspect of Malchus</t>
    <t s="39">[similar to the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt</t>
    <t s="40">(before the Splitting of the Sea)</t>
    <t s="41">which was "on the opening"],</t>
    <t s="42">and also the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea was only temporary,</t>
    <t s="43">for the revelation then was from Above, and the lower realm had no vessel for it,</t>
    <t s="44">in general, it is a matter of It'kafya and not It'hapcha</t>
    <t s="45">[similar to the Exodus from Egypt, which was in a manner of "for the people fled"].</t>
    <t s="46">Because this did not come from the service of the lower realm.</t>
    <t s="47">However, in the future there will be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="48">wonders even relative to the wonders that were in the Exodus from Egypt and the Splitting of the Sea,</t>
    <t s="49">that the revelation will be without any garment and also from the side of the lower realm,</t>
    <t s="50">and together with this there will also be the advantage of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="51">speedily in our days, literally,</t>
    <t s="52">with the coming of Moshiach our righteous one.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
